jobs.title: Director of Partnerships
jobs.description:
About Harri

It's a great time to join Harri as we revolutionize the hospitality industry with our cutting-edge technology solutions for workforce management. We're an innovative, high-growth company with a global presence, dedicated to building strong partnerships and delivering measurable value to our customers.

We are excited to recruit for this pivotal Director of Partnerships role to ensure the continuous identification, negotiation, enablement, and growth of strategic partner networks within the Harri ecosystem. You will serve as the primary business representative for potential partners and a trusted subject matter expert, playing a key role in bringing strategic projects to market and driving overall revenue and channel growth.

What You'll Be Doing

As the Director of Partnerships, you will be responsible for strategic partnership development, including identification, negotiation, and enablement of new partners as well as overall portfolio management.

Your responsibilities will include:

Serving as a key member of the strategy and business development team to define and deliver on new strategic growth potential.
Proactively seeking out new revenue/partnership opportunities and evaluating prospects through market research, sales collaboration, and industry assessments.
Leading commercial negotiations and contract execution on all terms and agreements, including security reviews and integration requirements.
Creating partner-level go-to-market campaigns in collaboration with strategy, sales, and marketing teams.
Managing the ongoing partnership portfolio, assessing performance through data analytics, and delivering partner scorecards.
Acting as the primary business representative at industry trade shows, conferences, and networking events.
Serving as the primary point of contact between executive stakeholders and partners from project inception through completion.

More About You: What Can You Bring?

We are looking for an individual who is passionate about the Restaurant and HR Technology ecosystem with a proven track record of exceeding target goals and scaling partner programs. You will be passionate about delivering successful outcomes and possess:

3-5+ years in a partnership program management capacity.
Bachelor's degree strongly preferred or commensurate experience.
History of exceeding targets and driving channel business results.
Strong experience with Salesforce and other sales technologies and best practices for team enablement.
Excellent communication, presentation, and negotiation skills with the ability to bridge executives, cross-functional teams, and external partners.
Experience or background in HCM and/or the Hospitality/Service Industry is preferred.
An ambitious and self-motivated team player who thrives in a fast-paced environment and efficiently manages prospect pipelines.

When and Where You'll Be Doing It

This is a full-time position.

Location: New York; Hybrid.

Travel will be required on an as-needed basis.

The salary range for this position is $150,000 - $170,000 (USD), depending on experience.

This role reports directly to the CFO.

What Will You Get in Return?

Creating an environment which enables our people to thrive is crucial for us. Harri offers a comprehensive compensation structure designed to support you throughout your career here. You'll get:

Competitive salary within the stated range.
The opportunity to drive critical projects for a high-growth, innovative company.
Experience working in a fast-paced, global environment.
A collaborative and supportive team environment.

Equity, Diversity, and Inclusion

We're committed to building diverse talent at Harri and believe our strengths as a team come from having many unique perspectives. We value a healthy, vibrant, and inclusive organization that encourages everyone to be themselves at work. We are committed to valuing diversity and promoting equal opportunities for all and welcome applicants from all communities.

Please note this job description is not designed to cover or contain a complete listing of activities, duties or responsibilities that are required of the employee for this position. Duties, responsibilities and activities may change at any time.

jobs.title: Regional Director of Operations
jobs.description:
📣 We’re hiring a Regional Director of Operations – Oregon!

At Compass Senior Living, we are Guided by Goodness, Loyalty, Faith, and Fun. It’s our True North — guiding how we lead, the decisions we make, and how we care for one another.

We believe senior living communities can and should be places of vibrancy and life — places that create meaning and joy for elders, their families, and the team members who serve them.

And we are continuing to grow, evolve, and elevate.

We’re looking for an experienced Regional Director of Operations to help lead our Oregon communities and be part of what comes next for Compass.

At Compass, we believe people make all the difference. We place tremendous importance on culture and believe trusting relationships are the foundation for caring for one another. That means this role is about much more than overseeing operations.

We’re looking for a leader who will listen, support, coach, challenge, develop, and empower our community leaders while creating the accountability necessary to achieve exceptional results.

Our next RDO will help us:

- Develop and empower strong community leaders
- Build cultures where team members feel valued, supported, and connected to purpose
- Drive operational and financial excellence
- Strengthen occupancy, retention, compliance, and resident satisfaction
- Remove barriers and create solutions alongside our communities
- Foster meaningful connections with elders, families, and team members
- Continue raising the bar while protecting what makes Compass culture special

We are looking for someone with strong Assisted Living and Memory Care operational experience, multi-site or regional leadership experience, financial acumen, and a proven ability to develop people and drive results.

But experience alone isn't what makes someone a Compass leader.

We want someone who leads with heart and purpose. Someone who listens. Someone who believes in doing the right thing, even when it isn't the easiest thing. Someone who understands that strong performance and a strong culture aren't competing priorities — the best organizations create both.

At Compass, our elders inspire, motivate, guide, and direct us. As we work to create an empowering and caring culture for today's elders, we recognize that we're also creating the future for ourselves as elders-in-waiting.

If you are ready to help us continue building that future and your leadership is Guided by Goodness, Loyalty, Faith, and Fun, we would love to meet you.

🧭 Come find your True North with Compass Senior Living.

jobs.title: Utility Scale Development Director
jobs.description:
RWE Americas, LLC

To start as soon as possible, full time, permanent

Functional area:
Project Development

Remuneration:
Exempt

The Development Director, Utility-Scale Development - Central Region
at RWE Americas is a senior individual contributor responsible for initiating, developing, and acquiring utility-scale solar, wind, and energy storage projects in the United States and Canada. The Director independently leads complex projects and cross-functional project teams from greenfielding through start of construction and supports projects through commercial operation. The role has no direct reports and delivers results by applying advanced development expertise, influencing internal and external stakeholders, and driving alignment with RWE’s North American strategy.

Role Responsibilities:

Develop and oversee utility-scale solar, wind, and energy storage projects from greenfielding through start of construction, with accountability for schedule, budget, risk, and project value
Serve as project lead for complex or high-priority projects, directing large cross-functional teams of internal subject-matter experts and external consultants without direct people-management authority
Manage the full project lifecycle, including site due diligence, land control, environmental review and permitting, interconnection, engineering and preconstruction, energy yield, tax abatements, power marketing, financing support, and readiness for construction
Define project strategy and critical-path priorities by integrating market, transmission, permitting, land, technical, commercial, financial, and stakeholder considerations
Establish and manage project budgets, objectives, schedules, forecasts, decision points, and deliverables; prioritize development spending based on project economics, risk, and market attributes
Lead cost-estimating and EPC-bidding activities in collaboration with Preconstruction, Procurement, Engineering, and Finance to improve cost certainty and support investment decisions
Drive optimization of engineering design, constructability, commercial structure, and other technical and financial levers to strengthen project competitiveness and risk-adjusted returns
Identify, analyze, and resolve high-complexity issues involving land, grid access, permitting, community opposition, project design, commercial terms, or competing priorities, escalating material risks with recommended actions
Lead critical negotiations with landowners, utilities, transmission providers, regulators, governmental entities, consultants, contractors, and strategic partners
Understand the key drivers of project financial attractiveness and identify strong project locations in collaboration with RWE’s commercial, transmission, and technical teams
Lead due diligence for project acquisitions, divestitures, joint ventures, and other transactions in collaboration with RWE’s M&A and functional teams
Prepare executive-level presentations and investment recommendations and drive internal review and approval processes with clear articulation of project value, risks, tradeoffs, and required decisions
Support power marketing, financing, tax-equity, and transaction processes by providing project inputs, coordinating due diligence, and ensuring that development assumptions are accurate and supportable
Provide strategic and technical mentorship to Development Managers, Associates, and other colleagues; guide project work and share expertise without formal supervisory or performance-management responsibility
Actively shape Central Region development strategy and lead internal initiatives that improve development processes, tools, governance, standardization, and portfolio execution
Provide support during construction to resolve development-related issues and help ensure successful commercial operation

Job Requirements and Experience:

Bachelor's degree in engineering, business/economics, environmental science, planning, public policy, or a related field; advanced degree preferred
Minimum of 11 years of relevant work experience, including at least 4 years of utility-scale wind, solar, or battery storage development experience in the United States
Demonstrated success independently leading complex, capital-intensive energy or infrastructure projects through multiple development stages
Experience leading multidisciplinary project teams and managing external consultants, advisors, contractors, or strategic partners
Expert knowledge of utility-scale project development, including land acquisition, permitting, interconnection, engineering, preconstruction, stakeholder engagement, commercial structuring, budgeting, forecasting, and risk management
Exceptional project and portfolio management skills, including the ability to establish priorities, drive accountability, and deliver results across multiple complex workstreams
Proven ability to lead through influence, align diverse cross-functional stakeholders, and resolve disagreements without relying on direct reporting authority
Strong financial and commercial acumen, including the ability to assess project economics, development tradeoffs, capital requirements, and risk-adjusted value
Excellent analytical, negotiation, problem-solving, and decision-making skills, with the ability to develop practical solutions to ambiguous or high-impact issues
Excellent executive communication skills and the ability to translate detailed project information into concise recommendations for senior leadership
Strong interpersonal skills and demonstrated ability to build trusted relationships with landowners, communities, government officials, regulators, utilities, partners, and internal stakeholders from diverse backgrounds
Motivated self-starter who is goal-oriented, detail-oriented, adaptable, and capable of managing multiple priorities independently while contributing effectively as part of a team
Excellent proficiency with Microsoft Office applications, including Excel, Word, PowerPoint, Outlook, and Teams
Ability to travel up to 50%
This position is an office-based role with travel to other RWE Americas offices, project sites, public meetings, and field locations
Must be able to sit, walk, or stand for extended periods of time

Applicants must be legally authorized to work in the United States. RWE Americas is unable to sponsor or take over sponsorship of employment visas at this time.

Pay range:
The annual base salary range for this position in Illinois is $190,000 - $286,000. The listed salary range represents our good faith estimate for this position and represents the range for new hire salaries across all U.S locations. Please note that the salary information is a general guideline only. RWE considers factors such as (but not limited to) scope and responsibilities of the position, candidate’s education & work experience, training & certifications, and key skills as well as market and business considerations at the time of the offer.

Benefits offered:
Medical, Dental, Vision, Life Insurance, Short-Term Disability, Long-Term Disability, 401(k) match, Flexible Spending Accounts, EAP, Education Assistance, Parental Leave, Paid time off, and Holidays. Eligible employees also participate in short-term incentives, in addition to salary.

Apply with just a few clicks:
ad code 93276.
Any questions? Contact HR:
rwe_americas_recruiting@rwe.com

We look forward to meeting you. Of course, you can find us on LinkedIn, Instagram, Facebook, YouTube and Xing, too.

All qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to race, color, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity, religion, national origin, disability, veteran status, or other legally protected status.

RWE Americas, a subsidiary of RWE, is a US-based energy company that is helping to meet the growing demand for energy across the United States. Backed by RWE’s 125-year global legacy of managing diverse power assets, RWE Americas operates approximately 13 GW of power projects across 27 states. With a talented workforce of 2,000 employees, RWE Americas develops, constructs and operates wind, solar and battery storage projects that safely deliver affordable, reliable electricity to our customers. Committed to responsible development, RWE Americas invests in local and rural communities, creating jobs and partnering with stakeholders to support and strengthen the places where we live and work. Learn more about how RWE Americas is generating impact at americas.rwe.com.

At RWE Americas, we foster a culture defined by our Essential Behaviors – Have Courage, Create Impact and Actively Collaborate. We encourage bold thinking and continuous learning, and we value ownership, resilience and inclusion in everything we do. When you join us, you become part of a team that supports your development, respects your contributions and celebrates shared success. This is a place where you can grow your career and make a meaningful difference.
